change.title: feat(acp): open chat file paths in editor
change.description:
## Summary

ACP agent chat now recognizes file-path citations in prose and opens safe, resolvable files in Termul's editor on Ctrl/Cmd-click. It reuses the existing terminal resolver, preserves external-link confirmation, and keeps path handling desktop-only because the web client has no supported filesystem opener.

## Related Issue

Closes #329

Prior related work: merged PR #110 provides the terminal file-link behavior; no ACP chat implementation PR was found. Closed PR #417 is for #331, not this issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] feat: new feature
- [ ] fix: bug fix
- [ ] docs: documentation only
- [ ] style: formatting or non-functional styling changes
- [ ] refactor: internal cleanup with no behavior change
- [ ] perf: performance improvement
- [ ] test: adds or updates tests
- [ ] build: build or dependency changes
- [ ] ci: CI/CD workflow changes
- [ ] chore: maintenance or tooling
- [ ] revert: reverts a previous change

## What Changed

- Detects path-shaped prose tokens and converts them into internal marker links without rewriting existing markdown links or code blocks.
- Uses active session cwd/project root and `openFilePathFromTerminal`, including line/column navigation and root-boundary validation.
- Requires Ctrl/Cmd-click, shows errors for unresolved paths, and keeps external links behind the existing safety modal.
- Adds parser, punctuation, wrapper, and click behavior tests.

## How It Was Tested

- [x] `bun run ci` (Biome lint + format + imports, strict mode)
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun run test` — 2,516 passed; 4 unrelated suites fail loading `material-icon-theme/icons/3d.svg?raw` through the shared symlinked dependency setup
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (in src-tauri) — blocked by missing system GLib/DBus development packages
- [ ] `cargo test` (in src-tauri) — blocked by missing system GLib/DBus development packages
- [x] Manual verification completed
- [ ] Not applicable

## Screenshots or Recordings

Not included; this change is validated through focused tests and desktop-only behavior is gated by the Tauri runtime.

## CI & Review Gate

- [ ] All CI checks pass (PR Validation, Rust Checks, Build Verification, Security Scans)
- [ ] Code review comments from CodeRabbit / Claude have been addressed or resolved
- [ ] No unresolved review findings remain

## Checklist

- [x] My PR title follows the conventional commit format used by this repo
- [x] I linked the related issue or explained why none exists
- [x] I updated docs when needed
- [x] I added or updated tests when needed
- [x] I verified the change does not introduce unrelated modifications
- [x] I read AGENTS.md and followed the contributor guidelines
- [x] A human reviewed the complete diff before submission

* **New Features**
  * Chat messages now recognize file paths and make them interactive.
  * Ctrl/Cmd-clicking a detected file path opens it in the editor using the relevant project context.
  * Regular links continue to use the external-link confirmation flow.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved file-path detection by avoiding single-token filenames, URL fragments, and trailing punctuation.
  * Preserved existing links and code blocks during file-path conversion.

commits.message:
fix(file-explorer): stream filename search via rg --files to fix 0-count regression (gh-195)

The file-name search Tauri command used a synchronous single-threaded
std::fs::read_dir walk, which on large trees (and on Windows where rg's
multi-threaded walk is dramatically faster) made the 'Files' tab count
flash 0 and never recover before the user gave up. The content search
already used a multi-threaded ripgrep spawn; mirror that architecture
for filename search and add a pending indicator so the count is not
a misleading 0 while the first batch is in flight.

Changes:
- Replace search_file_names with search_file_names_stream + search_file_names_cancel
- Use rg --files --iglob '**/*{escaped_query}*' (escapes glob meta; ** for depth)
- Stream search-file-names-batch and search-file-names-done events
- Cap queries at MAX_SEARCH_QUERY_LEN (500) and surface the error
- Cancel the in-flight filename stream on every new search, root change,
  worktree change, and reset
- Mirror content-stream's error/truncated propagation in the store
- Render '…' while searchFileNameMatches is null; back to the real count
  on the first batch
- Reap the child, propagate non-zero exit status (other than 1), and
  detect stdout read errors via manual iterator loop
- Exclude Thumbs.db / desktop.ini / .DS_Store / .env

Closes gnoviawan/termul#195

fix(file-explorer): address review findings on streaming search (gh-195)

Apply 8 review patches from review-patches-triage.md to harden the
streaming file-search implementation that landed in 145935d:

* Split the over-broad RG_SPAWN_FAILED code into RG_SPAWN_FAILED (real
  spawn failure), RG_STDOUT_CAPTURE_FAILED (pipe-already-closed) and
  RG_STREAM_FAILED (catch-all for stdout I/O errors and non-zero rg
  exits other than the 'no matches' code 1).
* Wire the new `code` field through the shared FilesystemApi type and
  surface it in the renderer as `searchErrorCode`. Clear the slot in
  every state transition (setRootPath, setWorktreeRoot, resetSearch,
  searchInRoot early returns) so a stale code never leaks across
  searches.
* Make the content stream's spawn_blocking actually reap the child and
  propagate its exit status into the trailing done event, mirroring
  the filename stream.
* Return Cow<'_, str> from strip_verbatim_prefix to avoid per-line
  allocation in the rg-output hot path, and drop the unconditional
  trim_start() that was incorrectly stripping leading whitespace from
  relative paths.
* Replace void IPC cancel calls with .catch() handlers at all 6 sites
  so a stuck rg process is at least visible in the console.
* Move the searchRequestId capture in the unmount cancel useEffect
  from cleanup time to setup time, so a new search started between
  setup and cleanup is not wrongly cancelled.
* Drop the tautological 'chars().count()' test and add 4 Rust
  coverage tests pinning the argv builder and event serde shapes.
* Add 5 renderer regression tests (2 for the unmount cancel, 3 for
  the new searchErrorCode reset behavior) with the supporting
  vi.mock('@/lib/api') infrastructure and a static useFileExplorerStore
  import.

Verified: bun run ci (biome) clean, bun run typecheck clean,
bun run test 1692/1692 passing (3 new), cargo clippy -D warnings
clean, cargo test --lib 239/239 passing.

fix(pty): adapt to Cow<str> return from strip_verbatim_prefix

Upstream #352 added a call to `path_validation::strip_verbatim_prefix`
in pty/manager.rs assuming it returned `String`, but the gh-195 patch
round (e801aa3) changed the signature to `Cow<'_, str>` to avoid
per-line allocation in the rg-output hot path.

The cmd.cwd() call requires AsRef<OsStr> and the TerminalInstance /
TerminalInfo struct fields are typed as String, so the bare Cow
return no longer compiles. Add `.into_owned()` to materialize a
String at the single call site. This is the only use of
strip_verbatim_prefix in pty/, so a one-line fix is sufficient.

Verified: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, cargo
test --lib 239/239 passing.

fix(file-explorer): address CodeRabbit review on gh-195 PR #364

Apply 4 inline findings and 1 nitpick from CodeRabbit review:

* src-tauri/src/commands.rs: escape '{' and '}' in the filename search
  argv builder. ripgrep's --iglob uses globset, which treats {a,b} as
  alternation; the previous escape list (\*\?\[\]\\) was incomplete
  and a literal query containing braces could be parsed as a glob
  pattern. Test query and expected output updated to cover '{a,b}'.

* src-tauri/src/commands.rs: always publish the trailing filename
  batch, even when files.len() == last_batch_count == 0. The previous
  condition (files.len() != last_batch_count) skipped emission for
  zero-match results, so the renderer would only learn of the empty
  result via the trailing done event. The store has a fallback that
  clears the pending placeholder on done, but emitting the empty
  batch is consistent with the contract and reduces flicker.

* src/renderer/lib/tauri-filesystem-api.ts: onSearchFileNamesBatch
  callback's event type declares 'truncated: boolean' but the Rust
  SearchFileNamesBatchEvent emits it as Option<bool> (omitted on
  mid-stream batches). Mirror the shared type contract (already
  fixed in src/shared/types/ipc.types.ts in the patch round) into the
  local listen<> generic.

* src/renderer/lib/tauri-filesystem-api.ts: onSearchFileNamesDone
  callback's event type is missing the optional 'code' field that
  SearchFileNamesDoneEvent emits. Mirror it from the shared type
  contract.

* src/shared/types/ipc.types.ts: extract the duplicated error-code
  union into a single SearchStreamErrorCode type alias and apply it
  to both done event signatures. Also fix the stale JSDoc on the
  filename done event: 'RG_SPAWN_FAILED' no longer covers stdout
  capture / runtime failures — those are now RG_STDOUT_CAPTURE_FAILED
  and RG_STREAM_FAILED respectively.

Verified: bun run ci clean, bun run typecheck clean, bun run test
1696/1696 passing, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean,
cargo test --lib 239/239 passing.

fix(shortcut): prevent Ctrl+W closing tabs when Agent Launcher is open (#365)

The Ctrl+W (⌘+W on macOS) keyboard shortcut in WorkspaceLayout unconditionally
called closeActiveTab, which terminated the active terminal tab even when the
Agent Launcher overlay was visible. Per the issue report, this caused accidental
terminal termination when the user was in the middle of invoking the launcher.

Guard the closeTab action with the existing isAgentLauncherOpen state so the
shortcut is suppressed while the launcher overlay is shown. e.preventDefault()
is also gated to avoid swallowing the keypress when the launcher should receive
it.

Closes gnoviawan/termul#365

fix(shortcut): address CodeRabbit review on #365

Apply 2 inline findings from CodeRabbit on PR #364 commit 090b7da:

* WorkspaceLayout.tsx: move e.preventDefault() out of the isAgentLauncherOpen
  conditional so the OS/webview default close behavior is always suppressed
  for Ctrl+W / ⌘+W. The original placement only prevented default when the
  launcher was closed, leaving the OS free to act on the keypress when the
  launcher was open.

* src/shared/types/ipc.types.ts: fix a stale JSDoc on the
  onSearchContentDone.code field. It previously referenced
  SearchFileNamesDoneEvent by mistake; replace with a generic pointer to
  the SearchStreamErrorCode union that actually enumerates the values.

Verified: bun run typecheck clean.

Closes gnoviawan/termul#365

fix(shortcut): close both keyboard and menu Cmd+W paths when Agent Launcher is open (#365)

Apply 2 follow-up findings from CodeRabbit on the #365 fix that were
posted as outside-diff PR comments and not surfaced as inline threads:

* src/renderer/layouts/WorkspaceLayout.tsx — add isAgentLauncherOpen to
  the keydown effect dependency array (lines 1095-1119). The previous
  closure read the value at effect-setup time, leaving a stale handler
  that could bypass the guard after the launcher state changed mid-
  session.

* src/renderer/layouts/WorkspaceLayout.tsx — apply the same launcher-
  open guard to the menu:close-tab event listener (lines 595-600). On
  macOS the menu bar intercepts Cmd+W before the keydown handler
  fires, so the keyboard guard alone leaves a path that still closes
  the active tab when the launcher is open.

Verified: bun run typecheck clean.

Closes gnoviawan/termul#365

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/dev' into dev

fix(file-explorer): use theme primary color for SSH folder icons (#305)

The SSH and Remote file explorer folder icons were hardcoded to
text-blue-400, which did not follow the active color theme. When users
switched themes (Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord, light themes, etc.), the
folder icons stayed blue and no longer matched the rest of the UI.

Replace the hardcoded blue with text-primary so folder icons follow
the active theme's --primary CSS variable, matching how file icons
already use text-muted-foreground.

Affected files:
- src/renderer/components/ssh/RemoteFileExplorer.tsx (line 198)
- src/renderer/components/ssh/SSHFileExplorer.tsx (line 142)

The local file explorer (FileTreeNode.tsx) uses MaterialFileIcon
(SVG-based) and was not affected by this issue.

Closes gnoviawan/termul#305
Merge upstream/dev: stream filename search fix (#364)

fix(explorer): align Explorer header typography with Projects panel (#334)

The Explorer panel header used `font-semibold text-muted-foreground`
while the Projects sidebar header used `text-sidebar-foreground` without
semibold weight, making the workspace chrome feel inconsistent.

Update Explorer header classes to match Projects:
- Remove `font-semibold` (Projects header doesn't use it)
- Replace `text-muted-foreground` with `text-sidebar-foreground`
  (matches Projects header for visual consistency)

Closes gnoviawan/termul#334

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { findFilePathMatches } from '@/lib/file-path-links'
+import { filePathFromHref, filePathHref, remarkFilePathLinks } from './chat-markdown-file-links'
+
+describe('chat markdown file links', () => {
+  it('only linkifies path-shaped tokens', () => {
+    expect(findFilePathMatches('See src/App.tsx:42 and ./main.ts')).toEqual([
+      { text: 'src/App.tsx:42', start: 4 },
+      { text: './main.ts', start: 23 }
+    ])
+    expect(findFilePathMatches('https://example.com/src/App.tsx')).toEqual([])
+    expect(findFilePathMatches('(src/App.tsx:42)')).toEqual([{ text: 'src/App.tsx:42', start: 1 }])
+    expect(findFilePathMatches('See src/App.tsx:42,')).toEqual([
+      { text: 'src/App.tsx:42', start: 4 }
+    ])
+    expect(findFilePathMatches('(see src/App.tsx)')).toEqual([{ text: 'src/App.tsx', start: 5 }])
+  })
+
+  it('encodes and decodes path markers', () => {
+    const href = filePathHref('src/renderer/App.tsx:42')
+    expect(filePathFromHref(href)).toBe('src/renderer/App.tsx:42')
+    expect(filePathFromHref('https://example.com')).toBeNull()
+  })
+
+  it('linkifies prose paths but leaves links and code blocks unchanged', () => {
+    const tree = {
+      type: 'root',
+      children: [
+        { type: 'paragraph', children: [{ type: 'text', value: 'See src/App.tsx:42.' }] },
+        {
+          type: 'link',
+          url: 'https://example.com',
+          children: [{ type: 'text', value: 'src/App.tsx' }]
+        },
+        { type: 'code', value: 'src/App.tsx:42' }
+      ]
+    }
+
+    remarkFilePathLinks()(tree)
+
+    expect(tree.children[0].children[1]).toMatchObject({
+      type: 'link',
+      url: filePathHref('src/App.tsx:42')
+    })
+    expect(tree.children[1].url).toBe('https://example.com')
+    expect(tree.children[2].type).toBe('code')
+  })
+})
